text_blocks.snippet: Medications for myocardial infarction (MI), or heart attack, are used to restore blood flow, reduce heart strain, and prevent further complications. Common medications include aspirin, anticoagulants, antiplatelet agents, nitroglycerin, beta blockers, ACE inhibitors, and statins.

list.snippet: Aspirin: Reduces blood clotting, preventing further clot formation.
Anticoagulants (e.g., heparin, enoxaparin, bivalirudin): Further prevent blood clots from forming and growing.
Antiplatelet agents (e.g., clopidogrel, prasugrel, ticagrelor): Inhibit platelet aggregation, preventing blood clots.
